title: Revenue of $0.00 keeps its headline above an empty chart outline
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin).
  2. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
  3. You are in a location (workplace) with nothing in it: no work order, invoice, credit or clocked time (for example ZZAUTOTEST Empty Shop).
custom_steps:
1. Click Dashboard in the top menu with ZZAUTOTEST Empty Shop selected (Revenue on This Month).
  2. Read the Revenue headline and supporting line.
  3. Look at the trend-line area of the Revenue tile.
  4. Click View details on the Revenue tile and look at the Revenue chart that opens.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The headline stays "$0.00", a real zero, and the supporting line stays "0 Invoices".
  • Every day's revenue is zero, so instead of a flat line along the bottom the tile shows a dashed outline with a small line-chart icon in its middle, sitting where the trend line would be, under the $0.00 headline.
  • The full Revenue chart in the expanded panel looks as before (axis and month labels with no bars). It does not turn into the outline.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 4. Design canvas boards 15_Empty_Design and 15_Empty_Now (row 15); board 04_Revenue_After for the expanded chart.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-E2: “A tile whose headline is a real zero, such as "$0.00" on Revenue, keeps that headline and shows the placeholder under it.”
  • S4-R13: “A tile also shows the empty-chart placeholder when every point that has a value is zero.”
  • S4-R18: “The placeholder changes nothing else on the tile. The headline and the supporting line show their usual values.”
  • S4 context note (expanded charts): “The full chart inside an expanded tile, and the charts on the report pages (Story 11), are unchanged.”
